heroHeadline: Egypt Erupts Over Ethiopia's Plan for Three More Blue Nile Dams; Sisi Hosts Kushner in El Alamein as Gaza Ceasefire Phase Two Stalls; Inflation Climbs to 14.9%
heroSubtitle: Egypt reacted with fury on August 17, 2026 after Ethiopia's Water and Energy Minister announced plans for three additional Blue Nile dams beyond the completed GERD, with a government source calling it 'a dangerous intention' Egypt 'will not allow.' The escalation came a day after President Sisi hosted US presidential adviser Jared Kushner in El Alamein on August 16 to press for full implementation of the Gaza ceasefire, as a Hamas delegation held parallel talks with Egypt's intelligence chief in Cairo and Egypt joined seven other nations in a joint statement condemning Israel's rejection of the Gaza peace roadmap. On the economic front, CAPMAS reported annual urban inflation accelerated to 14.9% in July, up from 14.3% in June, even as the Central Bank held its policy rate steady for a third straight meeting. Sisi also extended Suez Canal Authority Chairman Osama Rabie's term for another year on August 12 and spoke by phone with Ukrainian President Zelenskyy on August 14 about bilateral trade and regional de-escalation.
footerNote: Data sourced from Egyptian official records, UNESCO, academic Egyptology research (Shaw, Lehner, Hawass), major international outlets, IMF, Human Rights Watch, and institutional analyses.
